entries.en: FCC authorizes SpaceX plan to put up to 1 million AI data-center satellites in orbit
entries.note: 批准時間為美東 11 月 25 日 12:55（17:55 UTC）；部署時程為 FCC 許可條件；反對方為 Amazon、Viasat 與美國天文學會。
entries.one_line_summary: 美國聯邦通訊委員會 11 月 25 日批准 SpaceX 在太空部署多達 100 萬顆 AI 資料中心衛星的計畫，要求首顆衛星 2033 年 11 月前升空、2040 年前完成全部部署；衛星將以雷射鏈路互連、運行於 500 至 1,002 公里軌道，Amazon、Viasat 與美國天文學會曾提出反對。
paras: SpaceX 提出名為 Starmind 的計畫，要把 AI 資料中心搬上太空：在軌道上部署大量衛星，直接在太空中提供 AI 運算能力，避開地面資料中心面臨的土地與電力瓶頸。
美國聯邦通訊委員會 11 月 25 日批准這項計畫，允許 SpaceX 部署多達 100 萬顆 AI 資料中心衛星。許可附帶明確的部署時程：首顆衛星須在 2033 年 11 月前升空，2035 年前完成 10%、2038 年前完成 50%、2040 年前完成全部部署。
技術上，衛星將運行於 500 至 1,002 公里高度的軌道，衛星之間以雷射鏈路互連，射頻通訊作為備援。如此龐大的星座規模，遠超過現有 Starlink 的部署量，也意味著太空軌道資源的競爭將進一步升溫。
Amazon、Viasat 與美國天文學會曾對此計畫提出反對，擔憂軌道擁擠、碰撞風險與對天文觀測的干擾。FCC 仍予放行，這是監管機構首次為軌道 AI 資料中心開綠燈，也為其他業者跟進太空算力鋪路。

entries.summary_en: SpaceX has proposed a plan called Starmind to move AI data centers into space, using satellites in orbit to provide computing power. The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) approved the plan on Nov 25, allowing SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI data-center satellites. The authorization comes with a deployment schedule: the first satellite must launch by November 2033, 10% by 2035, 50% by 2038, and the full constellation by 2040. The satellites will operate in orbits 500 to 1,002 kilometers high, linked by laser connections with radio frequency as backup. Amazon, Viasat, and the American Astronomical Society had objected to the plan, citing orbital congestion and interference with astronomical observations; the FCC approved it anyway, marking the formal entry of space-based computing into the regulatory arena.
paras_en: SpaceX has proposed a plan called Starmind to move AI data centers into space: deploying a large number of satellites in orbit to provide AI computing power directly from space, sidestepping the land and power bottlenecks facing ground-based data centers.

The U.S. Federal Communications Commission approved the plan on Nov 25, allowing SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI data-center satellites. The authorization comes with a clear deployment schedule: the first satellite must launch by November 2033, 10% by 2035, 50% by 2038, and the full constellation by 2040.

Technically, the satellites will operate in orbits 500 to 1,002 kilometers high, linked to one another by laser connections, with radio-frequency communications as backup. A constellation of this scale far exceeds the current Starlink deployment and means competition for orbital resources will intensify further.

Amazon, Viasat, and the American Astronomical Society had objected to the plan, citing orbital congestion, collision risk, and interference with astronomical observations. The FCC approved it anyway, the first time a regulator has green-lit an orbital AI data center, paving the way for other companies to follow into space-based computing.

The satellites will be linked by laser connections and operate in orbits 500 to 1,002 kilometers high; Amazon, Viasat, and the American Astronomical Society had objected to the plan.

entries.one_line_summary: Google 的 AI 數學代理 Cogentic 11 月 25 日在 GitHub 一口氣發表六篇數學論文，宣稱在無條件整數分解上取得 L[1/3, 105] 的證明界，大幅推進 1992 年 Lenstra–Pomerance 的 L[1/2] 紀錄；六篇皆未經同行評審，Lean 4 證明已承諾但尚未公開。
paras: Google 的 AI 數學代理 Cogentic 11 月 25 日在 GitHub 公開六篇數學論文，涵蓋整數分解、離散對數、賽局理論與圖論。Cogentic 是 Google 內部以 AI 代理自動探索數學問題的研究計畫。
最受矚目的是整數分解論文：宣稱在無條件設定下取得 L[1/3, 105] 的證明界，大幅推進 1992 年 Lenstra–Pomerance 以來的 L[1/2] 紀錄。整數分解的難度是 RSA 等公鑰密碼學的安全基礎，因此任何進展都格外引人注目。
其餘五篇分別處理確定性分解的 L[3/4] 界、離散對數問題、奈許均衡的 1/5 近似、對數秩（log-rank）的改進，以及 Harary 邊重建問題。不過六篇論文皆未經同行評審，Lean 4 形式化證明已承諾但尚未公開，學界仍在等待驗證。
需要特別說明的是，L[1/3, 105] 是證明理論上的推進，常數 105 遠大於數域篩法的約 1.92，實際分解並未因此變快，也不構成對現有加密的威脅。GitHub 倉庫亦註明「這不是 Google 官方產品」，顯示這仍是研究性質的探索。

entries.summary_en: Google's AI math agent Cogentic published six math papers on GitHub on Nov 25, covering integer factorization, discrete logarithms, game theory, and graph theory. The most eye-catching is the integer-factorization paper, which claims an unconditional proven bound of L[1/3, 105], a major advance over the L[1/2] record set by Lenstra–Pomerance in 1992. The other papers cover a deterministic factoring bound of L[3/4], discrete logarithms, a 1/5-approximation for Nash equilibria, an improvement on log-rank, and the Harary edge-reconstruction problem. Importantly, this is an advance in proof theory, not a faster attack: the constant 105 is far larger than the number field sieve's roughly 1.92, so actual factoring has not become faster. None of the six papers has been peer-reviewed, the promised Lean 4 formal proofs have not yet been made public, and the repository notes that "this is not an official Google product."
paras_en: Google's AI math agent Cogentic published six math papers on GitHub on Nov 25, covering integer factorization, discrete logarithms, game theory, and graph theory. Cogentic is a Google research program in which AI agents autonomously explore mathematical problems.

The most eye-catching is the integer-factorization paper, which claims an unconditional proven bound of L[1/3, 105], a major advance over the L[1/2] record set by Lenstra–Pomerance in 1992. The difficulty of integer factorization is the security foundation of public-key cryptography such as RSA, so any progress draws exceptional attention.

The other five papers address a deterministic factoring bound of L[3/4], the discrete logarithm problem, a 1/5-approximation for Nash equilibria, an improvement on log-rank, and the Harary edge-reconstruction problem. However, none of the six papers has been peer-reviewed, and the promised Lean 4 formal proofs have not yet been made public, so the academic community is still awaiting verification.

It is important to note that L[1/3, 105] is an advance in proof theory: the constant 105 is far larger than the number field sieve's roughly 1.92, so actual factoring has not become faster, and it poses no threat to existing encryption. The GitHub repository also notes that "this is not an official Google product," indicating that this remains research-oriented exploration.
entries.one_line_summary_en: Google's AI math agent Cogentic published six math papers on GitHub on Nov 25, claiming an unconditional proven bound of L[1/3, 105] for integer factorization, a major advance over the L[1/2] record set by Lenstra–Pomerance in 1992. None of the six papers has been peer-reviewed, and the promised Lean 4 proofs have not yet been made public.

entries.one_line_summary: 小鵬汽車 11 月 25 日在第八屆科技日宣布，人形機器人 IRON 將於 2027 年 1 月量產，2027 年第一季先進門市擔任銷售導購「實習」，第二季正式發布；IRON 身高 170 公分、重 62 公斤，具 76 個自由度、1,500 多個觸覺點，搭載 3 顆圖靈 AI 晶片、算力 2,250 TOPS。
paras: 小鵬汽車 11 月 25 日下午在廣州舉行的第八屆小鵬科技日上，宣布人形機器人 IRON 的量產與上市時程：2027 年 1 月開始量產。
按照規劃，IRON 將在 2027 年第一季先進入小鵬門市，擔任銷售導購「實習」，在真實門市環境中接待顧客；2027 年第二季正式發布。這種「先實習、後發布」的安排，讓機器人在受控場景中先累積實戰經驗。
硬體規格方面，IRON 身高 170 公分、重 62 公斤，具備 76 個自由度與 1,500 多個觸覺點，搭載 3 顆圖靈 AI 晶片，總算力達 2,250 TOPS。觸覺點的數量顯示小鵬強調精細操作能力，而非僅止於行走與展示。
小鵬同時宣布，第二代 VLA（視覺語言動作模型）將於 2027 年上半年在全球首批交付。VLA 是讓機器人理解指令、看見環境並執行動作的關鍵模型，其進度將直接決定 IRON 在門市的實際表現。

entries.summary_en: XPeng announced the mass-production timeline for its humanoid robot IRON at the 8th XPeng Tech Day in Guangzhou on the afternoon of Nov 25: mass production begins in January 2027, IRON will start "interning" as a sales guide in stores in the first quarter of 2027, and the official launch follows in the second quarter. IRON stands 170 cm tall, weighs 62 kg, has 76 degrees of freedom and more than 1,500 touch points, and carries three Turing AI chips with a combined 2,250 TOPS of computing power. XPeng also announced that its second-generation VLA (vision-language-action) model will begin its first global deliveries in the first half of 2027. From mass production to store internship to official launch, XPeng has laid out a clear commercialization timeline, taking its humanoid robot from demonstration to the sales floor.
paras_en: XPeng announced the mass-production and launch timeline for its humanoid robot IRON at the 8th XPeng Tech Day in Guangzhou on the afternoon of Nov 25: mass production begins in January 2027.

Under the plan, IRON will first enter XPeng stores in the first quarter of 2027 to "intern" as a sales guide, serving customers in a real retail environment, with the official launch following in the second quarter of 2027. This "intern first, launch later" arrangement lets the robot accumulate real-world experience in a controlled setting.

On hardware, IRON stands 170 cm tall, weighs 62 kg, has 76 degrees of freedom and more than 1,500 touch points, and carries three Turing AI chips with a combined 2,250 TOPS. The number of touch points shows XPeng is emphasizing fine manipulation, not just walking and display.

XPeng also announced that its second-generation VLA (vision-language-action) model will begin its first global deliveries in the first half of 2027. VLA is the key model that lets a robot understand instructions, see its environment, and act, so its progress will directly determine how IRON performs in stores.

entries.summary_en: The European Commission proposed a Quantum Act on Nov 25, together with a sovereign tech equity fund with a target scale of €50 billion, aiming for Europe to lead quantum technology by 2030. The fund covers key areas including AI, quantum computing, semiconductors, and cybersecurity, and will give European firms preference in procurement to strengthen technological sovereignty. Importantly, €50 billion is a target scale, not an approved budget, and the fund is expected to become operational only at the start of the next multiannual financial framework (2028–2034). The proposal is the EU's latest response to the U.S.–China technology race, with actual legislation and funding still subject to discussion among member states and the European Parliament.
paras_en: The European Commission proposed a Quantum Act on Nov 25, together with a sovereign tech equity fund with a target scale of €50 billion, aiming for Europe to lead quantum technology by 2030.

The fund covers key areas including AI, quantum computing, semiconductors, and cybersecurity, positioning it as Europe's "sovereign tech" investment vehicle. The proposal also includes a procurement preference: public procurement will prioritize European firms to support domestic supply chains.

Importantly, €50 billion is a target scale, not an approved budget, and the fund is expected to become operational only at the start of the next multiannual financial framework (2028–2034). There is still a long legislative and negotiation road between the proposal and actual disbursement.

The proposal is the EU's latest response to the U.S.–China technology race: the United States advances AI and quantum through private capital and federal programs, China accelerates with national plans, and the EU is trying to close its investment gap with a public equity fund. Actual legislation and funding levels remain subject to discussion among member states and the European Parliament.

The background: API traffic grew roughly 1,800-fold from early 2024 to fall 2026, outgrowing the Python service, and by May 2026 Claude was already writing more than 80% of merged code. paras_en: Anthropic published an engineering post on Nov 25 describing how Claude agents led the rewrite of its Messages API from Python to Rust. The Messages API is the core interface for Claude's external services, carrying the vast majority of model-call traffic.

The background: API traffic grew roughly 1,800-fold from early 2024 to fall 2026, outgrowing the Python service, and by May 2026 Claude was already writing more than 80% of merged code. Rather than a simple language migration, this was a stress test of AI coding ability.

During the rewrite, Claude produced the first version of the core request path in about a week; the team used the production Python version as the oracle, shadowing live traffic to compare each case and ensure identical behavior between the old and new implementations. This "old version as oracle" approach is the key to a large migration that does not go wrong.

The result: about 70% less CPU per request and a median time-to-first-token roughly 20% faster, shipped without downtime and without freezing feature development. The figures are Anthropic's own; the engineering post itself has become the best demonstration of AI agents leading a large-scale refactor.

paras_en: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman announced on X on Nov 25 that Private Inference has entered limited customer trials. It is part of Private Intelligence, the program unveiled at DevDay on September 29, aimed at giving enterprises the confidence to hand sensitive data to OpenAI.

Technically it relies on confidential computing: prompts and responses remain encrypted inside attested environments while the model processes them, so even OpenAI cannot read the content during computation; once processing is complete, Zero Data Retention applies. This addresses a long-standing enterprise concern: when data is handed to a model provider, will it be seen?

Private Inference is currently an API preview, with applicable models and pricing undisclosed; it was previewed at an Azure conference on Nov 20. The trial is limited to a small group of customers, indicating that OpenAI is still validating the stability and performance cost of confidential computing.

For enterprise users, if Private Inference delivers on its promise, it will lower the barrier for highly regulated industries such as finance and healthcare to adopt external models; for OpenAI, it is also a trust chip in the contest with Anthropic and Google for the enterprise market.

entries.summary_en: MIT Technology Review reported on Nov 25 that AI startups have raised more than $100 million to harvest public records into AI sales intelligence, and the surge in requests is straining open-records systems across U.S. states. The figures: Starbridge raised $52 million and Pursuit $25.5 million; SmartProcure and Pursuit together file about 180,000 requests a year, and NationGraph submits about 10,000 a day for clients. The U.S. Department of Education's July log shows at least 29% of requests were at least partly AI-written and twice as long as before; Pennsylvania appeals reached about 6,000 in 2026, double the roughly 3,000 in 2021, with some containing hallucinated citations. paras_en: MIT Technology Review reported on Nov 25 that AI startups have raised more than $100 million to harvest public records into AI sales intelligence, and the surge in requests is straining open-records systems across U.S. states. Open-records laws were meant to let citizens oversee government; they have now become a data mine for AI companies.

The figures: Starbridge raised $52 million and Pursuit $25.5 million; SmartProcure and Pursuit together file about 180,000 requests a year, and NationGraph submits about 10,000 a day for clients. Most of these requests aim to obtain government procurement and contract information, which is then fed to AI sales tools.

The U.S. Department of Education's July log shows at least 29% of requests were at least partly AI-written and twice as long as before; Pennsylvania appeals reached about 6,000 in 2026, double the roughly 3,000 in 2021, with some containing hallucinated citations. Caseworkers are forced to spend more time distinguishing genuine requests from machine-generated ones, while real citizens' requests get crowded out.

States have begun to respond: California says AI systems are not members of the public, and Indiana lets agencies deny suspected scraping. The tug-of-war raises a new question: when AI can exercise citizens' rights at machine speed, how should the system distinguish "use" from "abuse"?
